### chunk_d5fc6ba72bf044d5b642f5b0ecff2255 (sequence 16)
- section_id: `sec_04b7d5127c39439b833215f57feb1d06`
- section_path: `2 Safety > 2.2 Intended use of engines and systems in Marine applications > Intended use`
- page range: `13`
- chunk_type: `technical_specification`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Intended use entails operation:
With fluids and lubricants approved by the manufacturer in accordance with the (→ Fluids and Lubricants Specifications of the manufacturer)
Within the permissible operating parameters in accordance with the (→ Technical data)
With preservation approved by the manufacturer in accordance with the (→ Preservation and Represervation Specifications of the manufacturer)
In the original as-delivered configuration or in a configuration approved by the manufacturer in writing (also applies to engine control/parameters)
With spare parts approved by the manufacturer in accordance with the (→ Spare Parts Catalog/Rolls-Royce Solutions contact/Service partner)
In compliance with all safety regulations and in adherence with all safety and warning notices in this manual
Work which requires communication with the control units must only be carried out with a diagnosis software or with tools approved by the manufacturer.
In compliance with the maintenance work and intervals specified in the (→ Maintenance Schedule) throughout the useful life of the product
In compliance with the maintenance and repair instructions contained in this manual, in particular with regard to the specified tightening torques
With appropriate safety guards covering all rotating and power transmitting components in accordance with applicable accident prevention regulations
With the exclusive use of technical personnel trained in commissioning, operation, maintenance and repair
The product must not be operated in explosive atmospheres unless the engine fulfills the conditions for such use and approval has been granted.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_2e5db4fb3aa5410a8622ec399fbb33e4 (sequence 17)

in explosive atmospheres unless the engine fulfills the conditions for such use and approval has been granted. Any other use, particularly misuse, is considered as being contrary to the intended purpose. Such improper use increases the risk of injury and damage when working with the product. The manufacturer shall not be held liable for any damage resulting from improper, non-intended use.
The engine shall not be allowed to exceed the admissible speed, e.g. when driven by an external source.
The characteristics of the deliverables are documented in this technical specification. Warranty coverage for any given purpose and guarantees of suitability for integration in any overall propulsion system or deployment in a fully integrated system shall only apply to the extent to which this has been expressly agreed in writing. No liability will be accepted for characteristics, specifications or deployment in any fully integrated system other than those expressly agreed.
The specifications of the manufacturer will be amended or supplemented as necessary. Prior to operation, make sure that the latest version is available. The latest version can be found on the web page:

### chunk_40f619e020524d03a823df0a69eb4b6d (sequence 25)

- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
All maintenance and repair work has been completed.

All personnel is clear of the danger zone surrounding moving parts of the machine. Electrically-actuated linkages may be set in motion when the Engine Control Unit (governor) is switched on.

All loose parts have been removed from rotating machine components.

All lines bearing media are ready for operation.

All protective devices are in place.

The walkways in the operating room are unobstructed and safe.

The operating room is adequately ventilated in all operating states.

No persons wearing pacemakers or any other active implanted medical devices (AIMD) are present.

In the first few hours of operation, the product emits gases as a result of smoldering e.g. lacquers or oil. These gases may be hazardous to health. Always wear respiratory protection in the operating room during this period.

The product is entirely free of damage, this applies in particular to lines and cabling.

The exhaust pipework is leak-tight and the gases are vented to atmosphere.

All components are properly grounded. Ground separately by means of a grounding stake as necessary.

Battery terminals, generator terminals or cables are protected against accidental contact.

The power supply (mains plug) is always freely accessible to facilitate disconnecting the device or system from the power supply at any time.

All connections have been correctly allocated e.g. +/- polarity, fuel line/reducing agent line, supply/return.
```

### chunk_1e1c96a373b54e60b42b1ba7daf1d0a0 (sequence 30)
- section_id: `sec_2a81bbd3e0ee4e75bc1917d14edb59e6`
- section_path: `2 Safety > 2.5 Safety regulations for assembly, maintenance, and repair work`
- page range: `17`
- chunk_type: `installation_instruction`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Safety regulations for work prior to assembly, maintenance and repair

Have assembly, maintenance or repair work carried out by qualified and authorized personnel only.

Allow the product to cool down to less than 50 °C (risk of explosion from oil vapors, fluids and lubricants, risk of burning/scalding).

Relieve pressure in fluid and lubricant systems and compressed-air lines which are to be opened. Use suitable containers of adequate capacity to catch fluids and lubricants.

Release residual pressure before removing a component in the supply line. To depressurize pressurized lines, shut off lines first, then release residual pressure.

Work may only be carried out on lines when they are free of fluids and lubricants.

Ensure adequate ventilation of the operating room when carrying out an oil change, working on the gaseous/ liquid fuel system or working with process materials (e.g. adhesive, cleaner).

Never carry out assembly, maintenance, or repair work with the product in operation, unless:

Expressly permitted to do so following a written procedure.

Secure the product to preclude undesired starting (LOTO), e.g.

Key switch

Start interlock

Close supply line for hydraulic starting

Close main valve on compressed-air system and vent compressed-air line when air starters are fitted.

Attach a 'Do not operate' sign in the operating area or on control equipment.

Disconnect battery cables or actuate the battery isolator switch, if applicable. Lockout circuit breakers.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

Use recommended special tools or suitable equivalents when instructed to do so.

Safety regulations when performing assembly, maintenance and repair work

### chunk_c12121ebf8574babb10419bc9bf1dbae (sequence 33)
- section_id: `sec_373adf2aa6bf47c89be4c586d21be35d`

Carry out work only on assemblies or plants which are properly secured.

Use appropriate rigging and lifting equipment for all components. Use all specified attachment points and observe the center of gravity.

Never stand beneath a suspended load.

Never work on engines or components when they are held in place by lifting equipment.

Make sure components or assemblies are placed on stable surfaces and secured against toppling over or rolling away. Adopt suitable measures to prevent components/tools from falling down.

|

|

Assume a safe standing position when performing assembly work.

Never use the product as a climbing aid.

When working high on the equipment, always use suitable ladders and work platforms. Special instructions for exterior components: There must be no risk of slipping e.g. due to icing.
```

### chunk_d473b4f40c3f4ebaa23793d1626c25b8 (sequence 34)
- section_id: `sec_84c5682220cd49f8937eee9b89b17621`

- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Pay particular attention to cleanliness at all times.

Completely wipe up escaped fluids and lubricants to prevent the risk of slipping.

Take special care when removing ventilation or plug screws from the product.

Ensure that O-rings are not installed in a skewed/twisted condition.

Carry out appropriate cleaning procedures to clean and inspect components requiring special cleanness (e.g. components carrying oil, fuel, or air).

Note cooling time for components which are heated for installation or removal (risk of burning).

Ensure that all mounts and dampers are installed correctly.

Remove any accumulation of condensate after assembling chilled components. Coat the components with a suitable corrosion inhibitor as necessary.
```

### chunk_15ff19b589b546ddbe5daff08388a025 (sequence 36)
- section_id: `sec_c8381f9d24294602be49a3e2934ffca9`
- section_path: `2 Safety > 2.5 Safety regulations for assembly, maintenance, and repair work > Lines`
- page range: `18`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:

Ensure that lines for all fluids and lubricants and their connections are clean.

Always seal connections with caps or covers if a line is removed or opened.

Fit new seals when re-installing lines.

Avoid bending or otherwise damaging lines, particularly the fuel lines.

Ensure that the lines for all fluids and lubricants have sufficient play to avoid contact with other components. Do not route fuel or oil lines near hot components.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_9bc04b0566a74429a8ea31f5bffe7496 (sequence 37)
- section_id: `sec_9e4030b8821d4ab890be448375e050a1`
- section_path: `2 Safety > 2.5 Safety regulations for assembly, maintenance, and repair work > Miscellaneous`
- page range: `18 -> 19`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Follow good hygiene practices, e.g. washing hands after work and before eating.

Ensure sufficient ventilation when working.

Do not touch elastomer seals (e.g. Viton sealing rings) with your bare hands if they have a carbonized or resinous appearance.

Do not paint elastomer components (e.g. engine mounts, damping elements, couplings and V-belts). Only install them after painting the engine or mask them prior to painting.

The following applies to starters with copper-beryllium alloy pinions:

Observe the safety data sheet.

Wear a respirator mask (filter class P3). Do not blow out the interior of the flywheel housing or the starter with compressed air. Clean the flywheel housing inside with a class H dust extraction device.

Safety regulations after performing assembly, maintenance and repair work

Before cranking the engine, make sure no one is in the danger zone around the engine.

Check that all access ports and apertures which have been opened to facilitate working are closed again.

All protective devices must be installed and all tools and loose parts must be removed, especially the barring tool.

Ensure that no unattached parts have been left in/on the product (e.g. rags and cable straps).

Ensure that the grounding system is properly connected.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_e0b7af8961d14aca90d21b20d90a29ef (sequence 38)
- section_id: `sec_f9340f44b5474044a11cf3755c581d2f`
- section_path: `2 Safety > 2.5 Safety regulations for assembly, maintenance, and repair work > Welding work`
- page range: `19`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Welding work on the product or any installed equipment may only be carried out by personnel authorized by Rolls-Royce Solutions. Cover the product when welding in its vicinity.

Before starting welding work:

Disconnect the battery cables or actuate the battery isolator switch.

Switch off the power supply master switch.

Separate the electrical ground of electronic equipment from the ground of the unit.

No other assembly, maintenance, or repair work may be carried out in the vicinity of the product while welding is in progress. There is a risk of explosion or fire due to oil vapors or highly flammable fluids and lubricants.

Do not use the product as ground terminal.

Never position the welding power supply cable adjacent to, or across the wiring harnesses of the product. The welding current can induce interfering voltages in the wiring harnesses which may damage the electrical system.

Remove components (e.g. exhaust pipe) from the product before performing necessary welding work.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_a17184b8331d411082f0d362e8f244c5 (sequence 39)
- section_id: `sec_3a4ccd3320f24155a04788ebd653d287`
- section_path: `2 Safety > 2.5 Safety regulations for assembly, maintenance, and repair work > Hydraulic installation and removal`
- page range: `19`
- chunk_type: `installation_instruction`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Check the function and safe operating condition of tools and jigs being used. Use only the specified jigs for hydraulic removal/installation procedures.

Observe the max. permissible push-on pressure specified for the equipment.

Do not attempt to bend or apply force to lines which are under pressure.

Before starting work, pay attention to the following:

For hydraulic installation, screw on the jig with the piston retracted

Vent the installation/removal jig, the pumps and the pipework at the relevant designated points

For hydraulic removal, screw on the jig with the piston extended

For hydraulic installation/removal jigs with a central expansion pressure supply, screw the spindle into the shaft end until correct sealing is established.

During hydraulic installation and removal of components, ensure that nobody is standing in the immediate vicinity of the component being installed/removed.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_86b548213b284d8897412e10dc8be896 (sequence 40)
- section_id: `sec_2a81bbd3e0ee4e75bc1917d14edb59e6`
- section_path: `2 Safety > 2.5 Safety regulations for assembly, maintenance, and repair work`
- page range: `19 -> 20`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Observe the safety instructions of the manufacturer when working on batteries.

Gases released from the battery are explosive. Avoid sparks and naked flames.

Do not allow electrolyte to come into contact with skin or clothing.

Wear protective clothing, goggles and protective gloves.

Do not place objects on the battery.

Check correct polarity before connecting any cables to the battery. The battery may explode and spray acid if the battery terminals are connected incorrectly.

Working on electrical and electronic assemblies

Always obtain the permission of the person in charge before commencing any assembly, maintenance and repair work or switching off any part of the electronics required to do so.

De-energize the relevant areas prior to working on assemblies.

|

|

ESD (Electrostatic Discharge): Work on components which could be damaged by electrostatic discharge must always be carried out with appropriate equipment. Appropriate equipment includes electrically conductive work surfaces or antistatic wristbands.

Avoid damaging cabling during removal work. When reconnecting, ensure that cabling can not be damaged during operation by:

Chafing on components

Contact with sharp edges

Contact with hot surfaces.

Do not secure cabling on lines carrying fluids.

Do not use cable ties to secure lines.

Always use connector pliers to tighten union nuts on connectors.

Subject the device as well as the product to functional testing on completion of all repair work. The emergency stop function must be tested in particular. Check operation of the emergency stop functionality, which entails switching of the power supply to the engine governor, may only be carried out when the product is cold.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_6f640c245a4c4cdd803139681a84db5d (sequence 44)
- section_id: `sec_cab1910eb34441b6b015a4f8463919f0`
- section_path: `2 Safety > 2.6 Fire and environmental protection, indirect materials > Fire prevention and fire`
- page range: `21`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Flames, naked light and smoking are prohibited.

In the event of a fire, stop the fuel supply if this is possible without endangering personnel.

Manually-actuated equipment must be easily accessible to authorized personnel to facilitate stopping the fuel supply in the event of fire.

The product has hot surfaces that can ignite combustible gases and other substances in the surrounding area. The operating company must ensure that the product is installed and operated a sufficient distance away from danger sources and any existing safety instructions or recommendations must be observed. Products that comply with the SOLAS convention do not constitute such a danger.

Depending on the operating and ambient conditions, fuel temperatures above the flash point temperature are possible in the tank. This can lead to the creation of a dangerous potentially explosive atmosphere in the tank and makes suitable explosion protection measures necessary.

After working with combustible indirect materials (e.g. cleaning agents), ensure that the area is well ventilated. The resultant vapor/air mixture must be sufficiently diluted to avoid a potentially explosive atmosphere.

Immediately eliminate any fluid or lubricant leakage. Fluids or lubricants splashing on hot components can cause fires, so keep the product clean at all times. Remove accumulated dirt (e.g. leaves). Do not leave rags saturated with fluids and lubricants on the product. Do not store combustible materials near the product.

Incorrect refueling of the reducing agent system with fuel can lead to fires.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_4390dad4e67942688ee179252805d72b (sequence 45)
- section_id: `sec_cab1910eb34441b6b015a4f8463919f0`
- section_path: `2 Safety > 2.6 Fire and environmental protection, indirect materials > Fire prevention and fire`
- page range: `21`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Incorrect refueling of the reducing agent system with fuel can lead to fires.

Before welding, clean the areas to be welded with a nonflammable fluid. Do not carry out welding work on pipes and components carrying oil or fuel.

When starting the engine with an external power source, connect the ground lead last and remove it first. To avoid sparks in the vicinity of the battery, connect ground lead from external power source to ground lead of engine or to ground terminal of starter.

A risk of fire due to human error or a technical defect cannot be excluded completely. Always have suitable extinguishing agents (fire extinguishers) on hand and familiarize yourself fully with their handling.

For safety-critical environments, check whether further fire prevention measures are necessary.

Toxic substances may be created during a fire. Always wear protective gloves and any other personal protective equipment that may be necessary when touching any components.
```

- content:
```text
Indirect materials may also be hazardous or toxic. When handling indirect materials as well as other chemical substances, observe the information contained in the associated safety data sheet. The safety data sheet may be obtained from the relevant manufacturer or from Rolls-Royce Solutions.
Only fluids and lubricants approved by the manufacturer must be used in accordance with the Fluids and Lubricants Specifications. Request the most recent edition from the manufacturer.
|
When operating with biodiesel fuel: Component corrosion during longer engine service life. Follow the special instructions in the Fluids and Lubricants Specifications.
Contamination of indirect materials with reducing agent (e.g. AdBlue ® , DEF): Store indirect materials in separate containers and use separate drip trays. Even very slight contamination with reducing agent can lead to malfunctions in sensors and other components.
Used oil contains combustion residues that are harmful to health.
When handling used oil, protective gloves must be worn.
Wash affected areas after contact with used oil.
Particularly hazardous substances in our products are compiled in a list:
http://www.mtu-solutions.com → REACH Declaration
```

- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Unauthorized use of compressed air, e.g. forcing flammable liquids (hazard rating AI, AII and B) out of containers, risks causing an explosion.

Blowing compressed air into thin-walled containers (e.g. containers made of sheet metal, plastic or glass) for drying purposes or to check for leaks risks bursting them.

Wear goggles when blowing dirt off workpieces or blowing away swarf.

Pay special attention to the pressure in the compressed air system or pressure vessel.

Hose couplings and connections must be securely attached.

Consumers being connected must be suitable for this pressure. Appropriate pressure reducing and safety valves must be installed if the admissible pressure of the consumer is lower.

Provide the snout of the air nozzle with a protective disk (e.g. rubber disk).

Carrying out a leakage test as specified.

Release residual pressure before removing a compressed air device from the supply line. To depressurize compressed-air lines, shut off the lines first, then release the residual pressure.
```

After skin contact, wash affected body areas with plenty of water.

Remove any wet clothing immediately.

Contamination of reducing agent with other indirect materials: Store reducing agent in separate containers and use separate drip trays. ### chunk_cf8f6b0be09e4474aad64c696cf3a61a (sequence 78)
- section_id: `sec_e5bcbd6a055441ea8bed674adf2a71b7`
- section_path: `3 Transport > Lifting specifications`
- page range: `27 -> 28`
- chunk_type: `technical_specification`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
The engine-generator set must only be lifted with a crane.

The engine-generator set must not be lifted with a forklift truck.

The engine-generator set must be lifted by the marked lifting eyes on the base frame only. Ensure that the load is evenly distributed to all lifting eyes.

Do not use engine or generator lifting eyes to lift the engine-generator set.

For weight data and center of gravity of the drive unit (engine and generator), refer to the arrangement drawing of the relevant project or customer order. Also consider the weight specified on the nameplate of the engine and generator.

Use suitable transport and lifting gear only.

|

|

The sling must move freely in the hook. When attaching/detaching the slings, make sure that no handling hazards occur, e.g. points involving the risk of crushing, shearing, catching and impact. Make sure that the slings are not exposed to load from sharp-edged objects to avoid damage.

Increase stability by attaching additional stabilizer ropes at the lifting eyes of the engine and generator. Stabilizer ropes must not be subjected to load.

Remove any loose parts on the engine-generator set.

Raise the engine-generator set slowly. The lifting ropes or chains must not touch the engine-generator set.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_c80051a6ff854f4fac151dbf24c84f26 (sequence 79)
- section_id: `sec_e5bcbd6a055441ea8bed674adf2a71b7`
- section_path: `3 Transport > Lifting specifications`
- page range: `28`
- chunk_type: `technical_specification`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Only 2 slings from the crossbeam to the lifting gear may be considered to be load-carrying. This requirement is not applicable if it is ensured that the crossbeam uniformly distributes the load to additional slings or - if the load is not distributed uniformly - the permissible load of the individual slings is not exceeded.

For further information, refer to the works standard MTN5194 (→ Page 1035).

Transport locking device

Always install the transport locking devices on the resilient engine and generator mounts and the base frame mounting prior to transportation (→ Page 29), (→ Page 30).

Always install the crankshaft transport locking device to avoid damaging the engine by undesired movement of the crankshaft prior to transport (→ Page 32).

Remove all transport locking devices before putting into operation.

Transport

The engine-generator set must only be transported in installation position: max. permissible inclination 10°.

The regulations, standards, and codes for cargo lashing and transport security applicable at the time of the transport must be complied with in the relevant country of transport.

- content:
```text
Preconditions

☑ The engine must have been filled with engine coolant and engine oil.

Transport locking device

Note: The transport locking device protects the resilient engine and generator mounts from shocks and vibration damage during generator transport.

General notes on removing and installing transport locking devices:

Remove the transport locking device from all resilient mounts before putting the engine-generator set into operation.

The transport locking device must be installed on all resilient mounts according to the instructions before transport.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

- page range: `29`
- chunk_type: `installation_instruction`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Loosen nuts (2) on all outer rings of the mounts, unscrew screws (1) and remove them together with washers (3) and nuts (2).

Store removed transport locking device parts in a safe place for further use.

Remove transport locking devices (4) marked with signal color.

Installing transport locking device

Install transport locking devices (4) marked with signal color.

Screw in nuts (2) in stages evenly into cap and base of mounting element.

Insert screws (1) together with and washers (3) and nuts (2).

Mark engine and/or generator as 'locked for shipment'.
```

### chunk_7a5ebf19809842c79b13f7859fa003c4 (sequence 95)
- section_id: `sec_dbbd8cdf5824436ba3722f58649aff43`
- section_path: `3 Transport > 3.4 Transport locking device - Crankshaft`
- page range: `32`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Transport locking device

Note: The transport locking device on both sides protects the crankshaft bearings from shocks and possible vibration damage during engine transport.

For installation and removal of the transport locking device, follow the instructions below:

The transport locking device on both sides must remain installed as long as possible during engine installation in order to avoid damage.

If the engine is to be moved together with the generator, the transport locking device for the generator must also be installed.

Prior to every engine transport, the transport locking device must be reinstalled on both sides according to the instructions.

Always use the screws supplied with or installed in the transport locking device to secure it.

Starting or cranking the engine is allowed only with the transport locking device removed. If the generator is already installed on the engine, ensure that the transport locking device of the generator is also removed.

Removing guard plates and engine supports (if applicable) on driving end (KS)

Remove screws (2) on both sides from the flywheel housing (4) and take off with washers (1), guard plates and engine supports (3).

Store the removed parts of the transport locking device carefully for possible reuse.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

- section_id: `sec_bf590b04ea274a738f14d14766e74b0b`
- section_path: `5 Functional Description > 5.2 Engine > 5.2.1 Engine side and cylinder designations`
- page range: `42`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
1 Left engine side (A-side)

2 Engine free end in accordance with DIN ISO 1204 (KGS = Kupplungsgegenseite)

3 Right engine side (B-side)

4 Engine driving end in accordance with DIN ISO 1204 (KS = Kupplungsseite)

Engine sides are always designated (in accordance with DIN ISO 1204) as viewed from driving end (4).

For cylinder designation (in accordance with DIN ISO 1204), the letter "Ax" refers to the cylinders on the lefthand side of the engine (1) and letter "Bx" refers to the cylinders on the right-hand side (3). The cylinders of each bank are numbered consecutively, starting with x=1 at driving end (4).

The numbering of other engine components also starts with 1 at driving end (4).
```

### chunk_40194b1da2504dcbbf912ef1175e3b8d (sequence 126)
- section_id: `sec_f9f73deb31a64027bc15b2d31a238b35`
- section_path: `5 Functional Description > 5.2 Engine > 5.2.2 Product description > Engine Interface Module (EIM)`
- page range: `43 -> 44`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
|

|

The engine is a liquid-cooled four-stroke diesel engine with c.c.w. direction of rotation, direct injection, sequential turbocharging and charge-air cooling.

An electronic management system provides engine control and monitoring.

Controlled by the engine electronics, the common rail injection system determines injection pressure, timing, and quantity independently of engine speed.

Injection pressures up to 1800 bar ensure optimum fuel injection and combustion conditions.

The charging system comprises charge-air system, exhaust system and sequential turbocharging.

The exhaust system is equipped with triple-walled, water-cooled exhaust lines.

Electronic control and monitoring system with integrated security and test system with interfaces to remote control system (RCS) and to monitoring system (MCS).

The Engine Interface Module (EIM) is the central connection box on the engine. It covers the complete minimum scope of a series marine engine. It has no controls or parts requiring maintenance.

|

Functions:

Battery-charging generator monitoring

Starter control (start repetition, tooth alignment, starter protection)

Open bus interface to the plant (SAE J1939)

Redundant power supply

Emergency stop function with wire break monitoring

Optional control of emergency air shut-off flaps

Interface to ECU and EMU

Key switch logic

MCS5 dialog interface

Connection for a Local Operating Station (LOS)

Control of a lube-oil priming pump (power unit in separate PPC Box)
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

- content:
```text
Data acquisition and data transmission

Rolls-Royce Solutions products automatically capture and record data and transmit it to the manufacturer. This does not apply to Rolls-Royce Solutions products in military applications.

The data transmitted includes operating data, GPS data, log files of malfunctions and fault messages. No personal data is collected and transmitted.

The data is used by the manufacturer for the purposes of product development and product improvement as well as for service optimization.

|

|
```

- section_path: `5 Functional Description > 5.4 Monitoring and Control > 5.4.1 System overview and features`

- content:
```text
EIM = Engine Interface Module

Installed on the engine

Start-air pressure monitoring, starting sequence, starter control, start interlocks, start repeat

Engine start:

Engine stop:

Emergency engine stop control

Stopping sequence, automatic safety shutdown

Coolant level monitoring

Engine Control Unit ECU 7

ECU = Engine Control Unit

Installed on the engine

All sensors and actuators are directly connected to the Engine Control Unit. Sensor failure, sensor function and cabling damage are monitored.

Engine management and closed-loop control, open-loop control and monitoring of engine values

Closed-loop control

Injection (fuel pressure, injection time, injection duration, operating status)

Speed (as per setpoint signals)

Controller

Emergency stop by engine protection system

Sequential turbocharging (right exhaust turbocharger cut-in/out)

Monitoring of engine parameters

Engine Monitoring Unit EMU

EMU = Engine Monitoring Unit

Installed on the engine

The Engine Monitoring Unit monitors additional engine parameters.

The main variables for engine speed, lube oil pressure and coolant temperature are redundantly monitored parallel to the Engine Control Unit.

The sensors are directly connected to the Engine Monitoring Unit, sensor failure and cabling damage are monitored.
```

- content:
```text
| Item | Color | Inscription | Meaning/function |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | White | ENGINE SPEED INC- REASE | • Holding the pushbutton down increases engine speed. • Lit as long as the pushbutton is held down. |
| 2 | White | ENGINE SPEED DE- CREASE | • Holding the pushbutton down decreases engine speed. • Lit as long as the pushbutton is held down. |
| 3 | White | - | (Not assigned) |
| 4 | Green | - | (Not assigned) |
| 5 | Green | - | (Not assigned) |
| 6 | Green | - | (Not assigned) |
| 7 | White | START | • Pressing the pushbutton initiates engine start. • Lit during the starting sequence. |
| 8 | White | STOP | • Pressing the pushbutton initiates engine shutdown. • Lit during the stopping sequence and as long as the stop signal is applied. |
| 9 | White | - | (Not assigned) |
| 10 | Green | READY FOR OPERATION | • Pressing the pushbutton makes the Engine Control System ECS-5 of the power train concerned ready for operation. The operator thus cancels the manual start interlock. • Lit when power train is ready for operation. |
| 11 | Green | LOCAL CON- TROL | • Pressing the pushbutton activates Local mode. • Lit when Local mode is activated. |
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_8b26deb3b746402da2dc425dfa7cce2e (sequence 180)

- section_path: `5 Functional Description > 5.4 Monitoring and Control`

- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Function keys to operate the LCD display

Additional displays and indicators

5.4.3 Serial interface RS 422 of the LOP

The Local Operating Panel LOP communicates with those parts of the plant which are not described here via the RS422 interface.

The data is transmitted in the form of one of the following types of block:

Binary measurand block

Analog measurand block

Request block

Alarm block

The form, structure and content (interface parameter) of the blocks are specified exactly for GenoLine (→ (E532301/xx) Installation and Commissioning Instructions).

Hot components/surfaces.

### chunk_497a4f5c8960479e834cc404d54ff705 (sequence 222)
- section_id: `sec_13ae53b76a5d40dfb0cf5f85f1e35994`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.1 Operation > 7.1.8 After stopping the engine`

- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
☑ Preservation and Represervation Specifications (A001070/..) are available.

|

|

| Item | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Coolant circuit | Drain coolant (→ Page 212) if: • temperatures below zero are expected and the engine is put out of service for an extended period without antifreeze additive in the coolant; • the engine room is not heated; • the coolant is not kept at a suitable temperature; • the antifreeze concentration is insufficient for the engine-room temperature; • antifreeze concentration is 50% and engine-room temperature is below -40 °C. |
| Raw water | Drain • If freezing temperatures are to be expected and the engine is to remain out of service for an extended period. |
| Engine control system | Switch off. |
| Air intake and exhaust sys- tem | Out-of-service-period > 1 week • Seal engine's air and exhaust sides. |
| Engine | Out-of-service-period > 1 month • Preserve engine (→ Preservation and Represervation Specifications A001070/..). |
```

### chunk_c6954a3c2fc24927a2b41454033a4c1c (sequence 228)
- section_id: `sec_91f4dc9cf7fb48bbb1227b480b983980`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.1 Operation > 7.1.9 Plant - Cleaning`
- page range: `78 -> 79`
- chunk_type: `technical_specification`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Dispose of contaminated water according to national requirements.
Observe the valid version of the Fluids and Lubricants Specifications. Further approved cleaning agents may be used.
Carry out plant cleaning only in areas where an appropriate oil separator is provided (environmental protection).
The following requirements apply for cleaning the plant outside with a high-pressure cleaning unit:
Prior to putting the cleaning unit into operation, read the operating instructions of the high-pressure cleaning units carefully and observe the safety precautions.
The pressure of the high-pressure jet (cleaning jet) must not exceed 50 bar.
The temperature of the cleaning medium must not exceed 80 °C.
A minimum distance between spray nozzle and plant of 1 m must be observed.
For external cleaning with high-pressure jet, use a fan jet nozzle only.
Note: Never direct compressed air directly at electronic components.
Seal all openings in a suitable way.
Note:
Carry out external cleaning as follows:
Remove coarse dirt.
Observe the instructions from the manufacturer of the cleaner!
Use high-pressure jet to remove loosened dirt.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_86bf6b222a07417ab4a8a6421e67e756 (sequence 235)
- section_id: `sec_4c792657852c4d8bbd2b0c06fec19d40`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.1 Operation > 7.1.10 Supplementary instructions for commissioning - Leroy-Somer generator > Lubrication of rolling bearing on commissioning`
- page range: `80`
- chunk_type: `installation_instruction`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Note: Rolling bearings are prelubricated in the factory.

During the first hours of operation, monitor the bearing temperature and listen for whistling noises:

Relubricate rolling bearings before putting the generator into operation, refer to the documentation provided by the manufacturer (→ Page 969).

Grease rolling bearings immediately if whistling noises can be heard.

Knocking noises in the rolling bearings are normal and decrease when operating temperature is reached.

An increased temperature (between +10 °C and +20 °C) for approx. 24 h is normal.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

| Engine blocked (crankshaft can not be rotated by hand). | 1. Check start interlock (→ Page 241). 2. Contact Service. |
```

After finishing work on the engine, make sure that all safety devices are put back in place and all tools are removed from the engine.

Loosen screws (1) and remove end cover (2) from flywheel housing.

- page range: `138`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Release latch of connector X4.

Turn engine in unloaded condition: Press START button.

Remove connector from Engine Control Unit.

Let the engine turn until oil pressure is indicated.

Connect connector X4 to Engine Control Unit and latch in position.

Engine starting stops automatically when the max. admissible time has expired. Repeat this procedure after approx. 20 seconds as necessary.

|
```

### chunk_3622436d00ee4b4d8b6b3f9c01b8d3fb (sequence 436)
- section_id: `sec_873820f154ed4cb299a43b3b66cdec04`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.3 Cylinder Liner > 7.3.3.2 Cylinder liner - Instructions and comments on endoscopic and visual examination`
- page range: `141`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: `table_6c8487cb492c40f085a29effe50e0716`
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Table 2: Endoscopic examination - Terms used

Use the terms listed below to describe the condition of the cylinder-liner surface in the endoscopic examination report.

|

| Finding | Explanations/Action |
| --- | --- |
| Minor dirt scores | Minor dirt scores can occur during the assembly of a new engine (honing products, particles, broken-off burrs). Removed cylinders clearly show such scoring on the running surface under endoscope magnification. Cannot be felt with the fingernail. Findings not critical |
| Single scores | Clearly visible scores caused by hard particles. They usually start in the TDC area and cross through the honing pattern in the direction of stroke. Findings not critical |
| Scored area | These areas consist of scores of different length and depth next to one another. In most cases, they are found at the 6-o'clock and 12-o'clock positions (inlet/exhaust) along the transverse engine axis. Findings not critical |
| Polished area | Polished areas are on the running surface but almost the whole honing pattern is still visible. Polished areas appear brighter and more shiny than the surrounding running surface. Findings not critical |
| Bright area | Bright areas are on the running surface and show local removal of the honing pat- tern. Grooves from the honing process are not visible any more. |
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_cb3a73f1cf344df5a2cbbf2eab5ab403 (sequence 437)
- section_id: `sec_873820f154ed4cb299a43b3b66cdec04`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.3 Cylinder Liner > 7.3.3.2 Cylinder liner - Instructions and comments on endoscopic and visual examination`
- page range: `141`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: `table_6c8487cb492c40f085a29effe50e0716`
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Table 2: Endoscopic examination - Terms used

Use the terms listed below to describe the condition of the cylinder-liner surface in the endoscopic examination report.

|

| Finding | Explanations/Action |
| --- | --- |
| Discoloration | This is caused by oxidation (surface discoloration through oil or fuel) and temperatu- re differences around the liner. It appears rather darker within the honed structure in contrast to the bright metallic running surface. The honing pattern is undisturbed. Discolorations extend in stroke direction and may be interrupted. Findings not critical |
| Corrosion fields / spots | Corrosion fields / spots result from moisture (condensate) with the valves in the overlap (open) position. They are clearly visible due to the dark color of the honing groove bottom. This corrosion is not critical unless there is corrosion pitting. |
| Black lines | Black lines are a preliminary stage of burn marks. They are visible as a clear disco- loration from TDC to BDC in the running surface and the start of localized damage to the honing pattern. Cylinder liners with a large number of black lines around the running surface have limited service life and should be replaced. |
```

### chunk_9ae8cf00c0214355a5b0e1e4fb940f06 (sequence 438)
- section_id: `sec_873820f154ed4cb299a43b3b66cdec04`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.3 Cylinder Liner > 7.3.3.2 Cylinder liner - Instructions and comments on endoscopic and visual examination`
- page range: `141`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: `table_6c8487cb492c40f085a29effe50e0716`
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Table 2: Endoscopic examination - Terms used

Use the terms listed below to describe the condition of the cylinder-liner surface in the endoscopic examination report.

|

| Finding | Explanations/Action |
| --- | --- |
| Burn mark | These are caused by a disturbance in the liner / ring tribo system. Usually they run over the whole ring-travel area (TDC/BDC), starting at the first TDC-ring and beco- ming more visible from the second TDC-ring 2 onwards and less pronounced from TDC-ring 1. The honing pattern is usually no longer visible and displays a clearly defined (straight) edge to the undisturbed surface. The damaged surface is usually discolored. The circumferential length varies. Liners with burn marks starting in TDC ring 1 have to be replaced. |
| Seizure marks, scuf- fing | Irregular circumference lengths and depths. Can be caused either by the piston skirt or the piston crown. Material deposits on the liner (smears), heavy discoloration. Se- vere, visible scoring. Replace liner. |
| Cylinder liner wear in TDC area | Cylinder liner wear in the TDC area occurs when hydrodynamic friction between pis- ton rings and cylinder changes to mixed friction under maximum firing pressures. |
```

### chunk_2465d4aa0af641f88f7adc3b39a31a1a (sequence 459)
- section_id: `sec_9c74db000d524940b132d5c29abecf1f`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.5 Valve Drive > 7.3.5.1 Valve protrusion - Measurement > Step 2: Measure valve protrusion at valve stem with depth gauge`
- page range: `146`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Check TDC position of piston in cylinder A1:

If rocker arms on cylinder A1 are loaded, the piston is in overlap TDC.

If rocker arms on cylinder A1 are unloaded, the piston is in firing TDC.

Measure valve protrusion for each valve in two crankshaft positions (firing TDC and overlap TDC cylinder A1) according to the diagram. Diagram (→ Page 150).

Loosen adjusting screw (1) and remove valve bridge. Do not remove rocker arm (2).

Use depth gauge to measure distance (A) between valve stem end and cylinder head surface at injector bore.

Admissible wear: 2 mm.

The specified value for a new cylinder head: 93.8 mm.

Have the affected cylinder head replaced by expert personnel ahead of schedule if the measured value is > 95.8 mm.

Adjust valve clearance (→ Page 150)

Install valve bridge.
```

### chunk_f6616754a4a141d1b96553200b4c9e34 (sequence 480)
- section_id: `sec_2ee2035933f941fda98f4be24c411624`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.5 Valve Drive > 7.3.5.4 Valve clearance - Check and adjustment`
- page range: `151 -> 152`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Check TDC position of piston in cylinder A1:

If the rocker arms are under load on cylinder A1, the piston is in overlap TDC.

If the rocker arms are unloaded on cylinder A1, the piston is in firing TDC.

Check valve clearance with cold engine:

Exhaust valves (short rocker arm) = 0.5 mm

Inlet valves (long rocker arm) = 0.2 mm

Check all valve clearances in two crankshaft positions (firing TDC and overlap TDC of cylinder A1) as per diagram.

If the deviation from the setpoint value exceeds 0.1 mm, adjust valve clearance.

Use feeler gauge to determine the distance between valve bridge and rocker arm.

|

|

Adjusting valve clearance

Loosen locknut (1).

Set adjusting screw (2) with box wrench socket so that the specified valve clearance is provided.

Insert feeler gauge between valve bridge and rocker arm.

Feeler gauge must just pass through the gap.

Tighten locknut (1) to specified torque using a torque wrench, holding the adjusting screw (2) in place to prevent it from turning.

Replace or rectify adjusting screws (2) and locknuts (1) which do not move freely.

Check valve clearance.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

WARNING

Fuels are combustible and explosive.

Avoid open flames, electrical sparks and ignition sources.

Risk of fire and explosion!

Do not smoke.

Wear protective clothing, protective gloves, and safety glasses / facial protection.

Liquid or gaseous media, e.g. fuel, are poisonous.

Risk of fatal injury through swallowing; risk of poisoning through inhalation; irritation to eyes and skin!

Escaping vapors of highly volatile media, e.g. fuel or ether.

Seek medical attention immediately; do not induce vomiting.

Wear protective clothing, protective gloves, and safety glasses.

Do not inhale vapors or smoke.

If contact is made with skin, wash off with water and soap.

Keep the engine room well ventilated at all times.

Hot components/surfaces.

Allow the system to cool down to below 50 °C before beginning work.

Risk of burns!

Wear suitable protective equipment/thermal gloves.

Avoid unprotected contact with hot surfaces.

|

WARNING
```

|

Internal loads and residual pressures in the HP fuel system. Risk of flying parts when released. Risk of pressurized fuel spraying out.

Never work on the HP fuel system when the engine is running.

Risk of injury from flying parts and spraying fuel!

Wait at least 15 mins. to relieve pressure before opening the HP fuel system.

Always wear protective goggles / safety mask.

Only use specified tools and jigs.

Undo threaded connections slowly.

Contamination of components.

Observe manufacturer's instructions.

Damage to component!

Check components for special cleanliness.

Preparatory steps

Allow HP system to cool down.

Remove cylinder head cover (→ Page 148).

Shut off fuel supply to engine.
```

TIM-ID: 0000000925 - 048

Note:

Note that the system is pressurized.

Remove HP line (4).

Slowly release unions on HP line (4).

Note: When unscrewing adapter (3), the stored volume of the injector is drained.

Remove adapter (3).

Note: Components are sensitive.

Remove screw (2) and take off hold-down clamp (1).

Protect the contact surfaces of HP line (4) and adapter (3) at the cylinder head against damage.

Install installation/removal jig (1) on cylinder head.

Remove installation/removal jig (1).

Remove injector (2) with installation/removal jig (1).

Note: The sealing ring (4) that seals the combustion chamber must only be used once.

Remove sealing ring (4) from injector or use a self-made wire hook or magnet to take it out of the cylinder head and dispose of it properly.

Note: For reassembly:

Remove O-rings (3), O-ring (2), and damper ring (1) from injector.

|

|

Note: For new version of combustion chamber sealing ring

Using pliers (1), slightly compress combustion chamber sealing ring (2) and remove it from injector (3).

Clamp injector at hold-down clamp contact surface so that tip faces upward.

Clean contact face (4) of combustion chamber sealing ring (2) and check it for damage. If damage is found, replace injector (3).

Cover all connections and installation bores, or seal with suitable plugs.

Clean all contact and sealing surfaces.

Installing injector

Note: For new version of combustion chamber sealing ring

Position combustion chamber sealing ring (2) at injector tip.

Clamp injector at hold-down clamp contact surface so that tip faces upward.

Using a suitable tool (1), press combustion chamber sealing ring (2) downward (e.g. with A/F 17 socket wrench, length min. 20 mm) until combustion chamber sealing ring (2) fully contacts sealing surface (3).

Note:

Always replace sealing ring (1).

Ensure correct installation position of sealing ring (1).

Use assembly compound without solids.

Coat new sealing ring (1) with assembly compound (Kluthe Hakuform 30-15) and install bearing against injector.
```

### chunk_44dda07073d144ff8c0744db4b30b4d3 (sequence 513)
- section_id: `sec_ad3fea11b0f348a1ab376def09918179`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.7 Injection Valve / Injector > 7.3.7.2 Injector - Removal and installation (jacketed fuel system) > Installing injector`
- page range: `159`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Note: If the injector contact surface in the cylinder head is contaminated, clean the sealing face in the protective sleeve with a suitable special tool/milling cutter. When doing so, do not apply excessive pressure to avoid damaging the sealing surface. If the milling cutter is pressed with too much force into the seat of the injector, this can result in damage to the cylinder head.

Remove oil carbon from sealing face on cylinder head and protective sleeve by exerting minimal force on the milling cutter.

Note: When installing a new injector assembly, the damper ring is already installed. Coat damper ring with assembly compound.

Fit damper ring (1) on injector and coat with assembly compound (Molykote P 37).

Note: When installing a new injector assembly, the O-rings are already installed. Coat O-rings with assembly compound.

Fit new O-rings (3) and (2) on injector and coat with assembly compound (Kluthe Hakuform 30-15).

Note: Ensure that the sealing ring does not fall into the cooling sleeve.

Ensure that the sealing ring (4) is correctly seated.

Note: Ensure that the alignment of the HP line connection is correct.

Insert injector with hold-down clamp into cylinder head, ensuring it is straight, and press down until firm contact is made on the seat.

Coat screw head mating face and thread of screw (2) with engine oil.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

Place a suitable vessel underneath to collect the fuel.

Vent additional fuel filter at screw (1).

Remove vessel underneath for collecting the fuel.

- content:
```text
WARNING

Components are moving or rotating.

Operate the engine at low load only. Keep clear of the danger zone of the engine.

A high level of noise is produced when the system is running.

Wear suitable hearing protection.

Risk of hearing loss!

Fuel prefilter - Vacuum gage check

1 Pressure gage

3 Pointer, red

2 Trailing pointer, black

4 Reset button

B Display area, yellow

A Display area, white

C Display area, red

Important

If both filters are in operation, the pressure gage is not directly connected to the fuel flow and does not display correct values. The pressure gage only provides correct readings if one filter is cut in, while the second one is cut out.

Important

The pressure gage is intended for operation at vacuum conditions only. Should the filter be operated at positive pressure or should it be vented, the pressure gage should be replaced with a plug screw or a different pressure gage. Otherwise, the pressure gage could be damaged.

With the engine running, read off at pressure gage (1) the vacuum (contamination level) at the filter output indicated by the red pointer (3).

Switch over to second, clean filter (→ Page 166).

When the red pointer (3) is continuously in the yellow area (B) at the latest, or at a high flow rate moves into the red area (C):

Replace contaminated filter (→ Page 167).

The black trailing pointer (2) shows the maximum measured vacuum. It can be reset by turning the button (4).

|
```

### chunk_a029c116112947dc83f560c9ef6c3706 (sequence 551)
- section_id: `sec_fa7c0bd5cc3e44a8aa9154c6bff8c9a6`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.8 Fuel Filter > 7.3.8.4 Fuel prefilter - Change-over > Replacing filter element with the engine running`
- page range: `168`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Note: Only work on the respective cut-out filter.

Cut out the filter to be replaced (A or B) (→ Page 166).

Note: Do not open vent valves with an open-end wrench; always use an Allen key.

Unlock drain valve (5) by pressing on the valve knob and open it.

Open vent valves (4) of the filter to be replaced.

Drain water, contamination and fuel out of the filter.

Loosen all three screws (1) at the same time.

Close drain valve.

Note: Ensure that the water level probe incl. cabling is not damaged, disconnect if necessary.

Remove filter element (6) with spring.

Turn filter housing a little until the screws move out of their mounting points, and take off filter housing.

Insert new filter element in filter housing.

Tighten all three screws (1) hand-tight.

Moisten new O-ring with fuel, fit it, and place filter housing back in position.

Note: Tighten screws evenly (a maximum of half a rotation in each cycle).

Use a torque wrench to tighten all three screws (1) to specified tightening torque.

Open filling connection (3) and fill filter with fuel until fuel escapes from vent line (2).

Replace copper sealing ring, close filling connection (3) again and tighten to specified tightening torque.
```

- content:
```text
NOTICE

Incorrect disposal/handling of used fluids and lubricants, e.g. used oil.

Ensure that used fluids and lubricants are collected in sufficiently large collecting containers.

Environmental contamination possible!

Used fluids and lubricants must be disposed of in accordance with country-specific regulations.

Do not burn used oil or dispose of in fuel tank.

Damage to component!

For filter replacement with the engine running, operate the engine at low engine load.

Severe material damage!

The filter which is to be replaced must be cut out for a brief period only.

3-way cock switching positions

1 Both filters cut in (operating position)

3 Left-hand filter cut out

2 Right-hand filter cut out

Fuel filter - Replacement

Cut out the filter to be replaced. Pull engaging pin (1) and turn hexagon (5) at 3-way cock with open double ring spanner to the left or right.

Unscrew cut-out filter with oil filter wrench and pour fuel out of filter into vessel provided.

Provide a suitable container to catch the fuel.

Clean sealing surface on filter head.

Screw on fuel filter and tighten by hand.

Check sealing ring of the new filter and moisten it with fuel.

Replace second filter in the same way.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

Use personal protective equipment.
Coolant is hot and under pressure.
Let the engine cool down.
Wear protective clothing, gloves, and goggles / safety mask.
Coolant contains antifreeze and is toxic.
Avoid contact with eyes and skin.
Do not inhale vapors or mist, wear breathing protection.
Wear protective clothing, protective gloves and goggles/safety mask.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when working with antifreeze.
Wipe up escaped/spilled coolant immediately.
Closing the cover on the coolant expansion tank when the engine is warm. After starting the engine, the necessary coolant pressure cannot be built up.
Before closing the coolant expansion tank, make sure that the coolant has cooled down to below 40°C.
```

### chunk_362fb25631d348eea5d1a156e856047d (sequence 637)
- section_id: `sec_6d86162e857e45bf9b921c7fcac9cd79`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.10 Charge-Air Cooling > 7.3.10.4 Charge-air coolant - Filling > Filling charge-air coolant using pump`
- page range: `185`
- chunk_type: `technical_specification`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Fill expansion tank until overflow edge is reached.
Open drain valve and pump coolant into engine at 0.5 bar minimum.
Close drain valve.
Fit valve cover on filler neck and close.
Check proper condition of valve cover and clean sealing faces if required.
Start engine (→ Page 73).
Turn valve cover on coolant expansion tank counterclockwise to first stop and allow pressure to escape.
After the engine has run without load for 10 seconds, stop engine (→ Page 76).
Continue to turn valve cover counterclockwise and remove.
Fill in coolant in expansion tank until the coolant level at top edge of filler neck remains constant.
Check coolant level (→ Page 179) and top up as required:
Fit valve cover on filler neck and close.
Disconnect pump and hose.
Repeat the steps from Start engine (→ Step 7) until no more coolant has to be added.
```

Alternatively: Fill in coolant in expansion tank via filler neck until coolant level at top edge of filler neck remains constant.
Fit valve cover on filler neck and close until it engages (first lock).
Check proper condition of valve cover and clean sealing faces if required.
Start engine (→ Page 73).
Turn valve cover counterclockwise and remove.
After the engine has run without load for 10 seconds, stop engine (→ Page 76).
Check coolant level (→ Page 179) and top up as required:
Fit valve cover on filler neck and close.
Repeat the steps from Start engine (→ Step 4) until no more coolant has to be added.
Start engine and run it without load for some minutes.
Check coolant level (→ Page 179) and top up as required.
|
```

### chunk_06a5cc95d25b481a8f0002a2ade42959 (sequence 673)
- section_id: `sec_3894f5e2ccad4f8d8637be7a09a55546`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.13 Lube Oil System, Lube Oil Circuit > 7.3.13.1 Engine oil - Level check`
- page range: `192`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Note:

The engine oil circuit is equipped with an automatic oil replenishment system. During engine operation, the oil level in the engine oil pan is compensated (filled) continuously from the replenishment tank. In normal engine operation, the engine oil level is therefore only checked or topped up in the replenishment tank.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_b45832c6352b4157ad7e53a8d83ec82f (sequence 674)
- section_id: `sec_90a56b61054f4f8ea44b69a6afba7d68`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.13 Lube Oil System, Lube Oil Circuit > 7.3.13.1 Engine oil - Level check > Checking engine oil level in replenishment tank`
- page range: `192`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Check engine oil level in replenishment tank.

Fill replenishment tank up to the upper mark, if necessary.

Checking oil level at engine (prior to engine start)

Note: Engine is stopped and starting disabled.

Insert oil dipstick into guide tube up to the stop, pull it out after approx. 10 seconds and check oil level.

Pull out oil dipstick from guide tube and wipe it.

Note: The oil level may be up to 2 cm above the mark (1) after a longer out-of-service period. The reason for this may be oil returning to the oil pan e.g. from oil filters and heat exchangers.

Top up with oil to mark (1) as necessary (→ Page 193).

The oil level must reach the mark (1) or exceed the mark (1) by up to 2 cm.

Insert oil dipstick into guide tube up to the stop.

Checking oil level at engine (after stopping the engine)

Stop engine and disable engine start.

Insert oil dipstick into guide tube up to the stop, pull it out after approx. 10 seconds and check oil level.

5 minutes after stopping the engine, remove oil dipstick from guide tube and wipe it.

Oil level must be between marks (1) and (2).

Insert oil dipstick into guide tube up to the stop.

Top up with oil to mark (1) as necessary (→ Page 193).
```

Close drain cock on replenishment tank.

Switch the 3-way valve to the oil priming pump outlet connection at the engine.

Remove drain plugs (2) and (3) and drain oil:

WARNING

Engine oil - Sample extraction and analysis

Open drain plug (2) of automatic oil filter (1) by one to two rotations.

Drain approx. 1 liter of engine oil to flush out oil sludge.

Close drain plug (2).

Drain approx. 0.25 liters of engine oil into a clean vessel.

Using the equipment and chemicals of the diesel engine test kit, examine engine oil for:

Water content

Dispersancy (spot test)

Dilution by fuel

- section_id: `sec_16e0c4d0c9704f9d8bd1ee8aa63908e5`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.14 Oil Filtration / Cooling > 7.3.14.2 Oil indicator filter - Cleaning`

- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
|

Cleaning strainer

Important

Observe the valid version of the Fluids and Lubricants Specifications. Further approved cleaning agents may be used.

Shake coarse contamination out of strainer.

Use a soft brush to remove stubborn deposits from strainer if required. Ensure that the mesh is not damaged.

Clean all metallic parts with cleaner.

Carefully blow out strainer with compressed air from outside to inside.

Checking strainer

Check strainer for damage.

Fit new strainer if damaged or severely contaminated.

Installing strainer

Insert strainer with new O-ring into housing.

Install cover (1) with new O-ring.

Fill housing with new engine oil.
```

### chunk_152792080e7246518b51b81900914094 (sequence 723)
- section_id: `sec_3e33cd7c19fa4e4498d3c373836168b3`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.14 Oil Filtration / Cooling > 7.3.14.4 Oil indicator filter - Cleaning and check > Removing basket strainer - variant A`
- page range: `205`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Clean oil indicator filter before disassembling it.

Take off cover (2) and O-ring (3).

Remove screws (1).

Remove spring (4) and strainer (6) from filter housing and allow oil to drip into container.

Cleaning strainer

Important

Observe the valid version of the Fluids and Lubricants Specifications. Further approved cleaning agents may be used.

Shake coarse contamination out of strainer (6).

Clean all metallic parts with cleaner Hakutex 60 mtu.

Note: Do not damage the fabric of the strainer.

Blow out strainer (6) with compressed air from outside to inside.

Use a soft brush to remove stubborn deposits from strainer as necessary.

Checking strainer
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_352a399e79fd44c599c1f477b766d59f (sequence 724)
- section_id: `sec_3e33cd7c19fa4e4498d3c373836168b3`

- table_ids: `table_20f9fd58625e45e8bf0c99b3a54fb25a`
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Use a soft brush to remove stubborn deposits from strainer as necessary.

Coat square-section ring (5) on strainer (6) with engine oil and install strainer (6).

| Item | Findings | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Strainer | Metallic residues | • Clean • Monitor engine operation • Check strainer daily • Contact Service |

### chunk_d728e55d427c404ba4a10f2fe25f4c1f (sequence 735)
- section_id: `sec_7f8d4406d9c34216afe6820bdcdf035d`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.14 Oil Filtration / Cooling > 7.3.14.5 Centrifugal oil filter - Cleaning and filter-sleeve replacement`
- page range: `208`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Remove clamp (14).

Carefully lift rotor (11), allow oil to drain and remove from housing.

Loosen cover screw (2) and take off hood (1).

Holding the rotor (11) firmly, loosen rotor cover nut (3).

Remove filter sleeve (6).

Take off rotor cover (4).

Measure thickness of oil residues on filter sleeve (6).

Disassemble rotor pipe (7), conical disk (8) and rotor base (10).

Result: Shorten maintenance interval if the oil residues exceed the maximum thickness of 45 mm.

Wash rotor cover (4), rotor pipe (7), conical disk (8) and rotor base (10) with cold cleaner.

Check sealing ring (9), replace if necessary.

Blow out with compressed air.

Assemble rotor pipe (7), conical disk (8) and rotor base (10) with sealing ring (9).

Check sealing ring (5), replace if necessary.

Insert new filter sleeve (6) in rotor pipe (7) with the smooth paper surface facing the outer wall.

Install rotor cover (4) with sealing ring (5).

Use torque wrench to tighten rotor cover nut (3) to specified tightening torque.

Insert rotor (11) in housing (12) and check for ease of movement.

Place sealing ring (13) on housing (12).

Check sealing ring (13), replace if necessary.

Fit hood (1).

Tighten cover screw (2) by hand.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_36964a39f5614c518bb960c00d9e64ed (sequence 773)
- section_id: `sec_eea1e009604545338b882173c47bdbb0`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.15 Coolant Circuit, General, High-Temperature Circuit > 7.3.15.5 Engine coolant - Filling > Filling coolant`
- page range: `215`
- chunk_type: `technical_specification`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Open venting points, see figure.
Pumping in coolant via filling line:
5 Venting point, turbocharger, right
4 Venting point, turbocharger, left
6 Venting point, turbocharger, right
Fill with coolant. To do this, pump in coolant either via the filling line or fill into expansion tank:
Open shut-off cock of connection line for engine coolant filling/draining.
Close shut-off cock of connection line for engine coolant filling/draining.
Pump in coolant via the connection line for engine coolant filling/draining at base frame until the coolant level reaches the top edge of the filler neck at the expansion tank where it remains constant.
Fill in engine coolant via filler neck on expansion tank until engine coolant level remains constant at top edge of filler neck.
Check proper condition of valve cover and clean sealing faces if required.
Close venting points one by one when coolant emerges, proceeding from the lowest point upwards.
Set valve cover onto filler neck and turn until the first stop.
After 10 seconds of running the engine without load, shut down the engine (→ Page 76).
Start engine (→ Page 73).
Turn valve cover counterclockwise and remove.
Repeat the steps from "Start engine" (→ Step 6) until no more engine coolant needs to be topped up.
Check coolant level (→ Page 210) and top up engine coolant as required:
Check proper condition of valve cover and clean sealing faces if required.
```

### chunk_9740348df68649b98b1749a6dc1b6276 (sequence 815)
- section_id: `sec_4fd12446c77742f3b6676abaf1043ff3`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.18 Battery-Charging Generator > 7.3.18.1 Battery-charging generator drive - Coupling condition check`
- page range: `223`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Battery-charging generator drive, coupling condition check

Install barring tool (→ Page 136).

Guide endoscope optics between guard plate (1) and battery-charging generator carrier (2) (arrow).

Note: Seek the assistance of a second person

Examine the resilient coupling over the entire circumference for plastic deformation and cracks.

Bar engine slowly by hand.

If there is serious deformation or crack formation, contact Service.

Remove barring gear (→ Page 136).
```

Fit protective cap (2).

- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Engine mount - Measuring height of rubber element

A Unloaded 152.5 mm

C Serial number

B Preloaded 148.5 mm

D SHORE hardness

F Preloaded 28 ±0.3 mm

E Type

G Unloaded 50 mm

*** Height adjustment range 5±5 mm

H Locking plate 5 mm

Measure each resilient mount.

If the height (B) of a rubber element is below 140 mm: Replace relevant resilient mount (→ Page 544).

Measure the height (B) of the rubber elements under load:

If height differences between the resilient mounts of > 2 mm are measured: Balance out the height differences. To do this, place shims between the relevant resilient mount and the contact surface.
```

Preconditions

Electric voltage supply for operation.

Danger of burns and potentially fatal electric shock!

Coolant is hot and under pressure.

Let the engine cool down.

Risk of injury and scalding!

Wear protective clothing, gloves, and goggles / safety mask.

Coolant contains antifreeze and is toxic.

Avoid contact with eyes and skin.

Risk of poisoning and slipping!

Do not inhale vapors or mist, wear breathing protection.

Wear protective clothing, protective gloves and goggles/safety mask.

Do not eat, drink, smoke when working with antifreeze.

Wipe up escaped/spilled coolant immediately.

Heavy part, risk of falling or overturning due to lack of stability.

Use appropriate lifting gear and appliances.

Risk of crushing body or limbs!

Wear safety shoes.

DANGER

### chunk_ac4cb2fca8824e99a844ba9a844ba5df (sequence 847)
- section_id: `sec_823793f1eb2d43a0aa140b7a85b55043`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.21 Preheater > 7.3.21.3 Preheater - Overhaul > Overhauling preheater`
- page range: `231 -> 232`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Disconnect power supply of heating element.

Drain coolant at drain valve into a clean container.

Close shut-off valves in coolant lines before and after preheater.

Clean and flush coolant circuit.

Check cabling for damage and overheating.

Check hoses for cracks and other damage. Replace as necessary.

|

|

Allow heating element to cool down.

Remove screws of outlet box (4) and remove outlet box (4) and O-ring (3).

Remove housing cover (7).

Loosen thermostat clip (6).

Replace thermostat (5) as necessary.

Remove terminals on thermostat (5) from blade terminals of measuring unit.

Remove screws of heating element plate (2).

Remove heating element plate (2) with heating element (8) from tank (9).

Note: Make sure that O-ring (1) is properly installed.

Install heating element plate (2) with heating element (8).

Clean heating element (8) and tank (9).

Install outlet box (4) and O-ring (3).

Connect heating element to voltage supply.

Install housing cover (7).

Remove pump from volute and check for residues in impeller and lines.

Check preheater for leakage and correct operation (→ Page 230).

Connect hoses and open shut-off valves.

Check coolant level (→ Page 210).
```

- page range: `233`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Undo the screws on the control box (1) and open the control box.

Mark all cables (4) prior to disconnection.

Disconnect all cables (4) from solenoid switch (1).

Note: The solenoid switch is secured to the rail (2) by a spring clip (3).

Fit a new solenoid switch on the rail and fully engage the spring clip.

Pull out the spring clip with a screwdriver and slide the solenoid switch off the rail.

Connect up all wires as marked previously.

Close control box and tighten screws.
```

- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Perform one current measurement per phase with a clamp meter at an accessible location (e.g. in the control cabinet).

The actual current consumption may only be a bit lower.

For current consumption, see electrical documentation, or calculate according to formula: I = P / (√3 * U), I in amperes, P in watts, U in volts.

If there is a major deviation in current consumption, replace defective heating element(s), (→ contact Service).

|
```

### chunk_abb97a8b77c94c76ae7d0093d0546ed3 (sequence 873)
- section_id: `sec_8eeab99f4fd24cfebc68d8013295d6c4`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.22 Wiring (General) for Engine/Gearbox/Unit > 7.3.22.1 Engine wiring harness - Overview > Engine wiring harness for injectors 20V`
- page range: `240`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Engine cabling - Check

Check securing screws of cable clamps on engine and tighten loose screw connections.

Check if all cable clips are closed and intact.

Ensure that cables are securely seated in clamps and cannot move freely.

Replace faulty cable clips.

Replace faulty cable ties.

Check that cable ties are firmly seated, tighten loose cable ties.

Visually inspect the following electrical components for damage:

Contacts

Connector housings

Sockets

Plug-in contacts

Cables and terminals

Result: Contact Service if cable conductors are damaged.

Note: Close off disconnected connectors with protective caps provided.

Ensure that all connecting plugs of the sensors are correctly engaged.

Use isopropyl alcohol to clean dirty connector housings, sockets and contacts.

Important

Connecting connectors to sensors is only permitted when the engine is stopped.

|
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_6c408be1a88e4bbe8aafc334ba9fce2d (sequence 875)
- section_id: `sec_c70f2dc1fd1b458b83d848c05e49fcb9`
- section_path: `7 Operating Instructions > 7.3 Task Description > 7.3.23 Accessories for (Electronic) Engine Governor / Control System > 7.3.23.1 Limit switch for start interlock - Check`
- page range: `241`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Preconditions

☑ Engine is stopped and starting disabled.

Note: In the OFF position, the limit switch activates a start interlock, i.e. the engine cannot be started.

Limit switch for start interlock - Check

Check whether switches (3) and guard plate (2) with engine support (1) are installed on both sides of flywheel housing (4).

If switches (3) and/or guard plate (2) with engine support (1) is/are not installed:

Check whether both switches (3) are actuated.

Screw on guard plate (2) with engine support (1).

If switch (3) and guard plate (2) are installed, but switch (3) is in the OFF position:

Then screw on switch (3), ensuring that the switch (3) is actuated by the guard plate (2).

Make certain that the guard plate (2) at the side of the switch (3) is not distorted.

Loosen guard plate (2) and screw on such that the switch (3) is actuated.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

Mark installation positions with safety valve and oil filler neck.

### chunk_7e790b4a87b84f188aa3fdace94cce57 (sequence 940)
- section_id: `sec_88875209b1eb47c1a1c73dbd9d3e9f57`
- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.1 Crankcase and Attachments > 8.1.10 Cylinder liner - Removal`
- page range: `261`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Note:

Mark installation position of cylinder liner in relation to crankcase (arrow) with a marking pen.

Removing cylinder liner

A marking of the installation position of the cylinder liner must only be applied if the liner is intended to be re-installed. Piston and cylinder liner are paired and must not be separated.

Note: If oil spray nozzle is not removed, take care not to damage it. With the crankshaft installed, ensure that the tool does not butt against the crankshaft (turn crankshaft if necessary).

Install puller on crankcase bores.

Insert puller into cylinder liner (1) and place the two shoulders of the puller plate (2) exactly onto the lower collar of the cylinder liner (1).

Coat nut (3) and threaded rod with engine oil.

Remove puller.

Holding the hexagon of the threaded rod firmly, turn nut (3) of puller until cylinder liner (1) is released from crankcase bore.

Remove cylinder liner (1) from crankcase.

Remove sealing rings from cylinder liner (1).
```

Degrease and dry-clean cylinder liner on lower fit surface and slip chamfer.

Coat sealing rings (1) with assembly compound.

Fit sealing rings (1) on grooves of cylinder liner.

Position cylinder liner at bore.

Insert new cylinder liner in any installation position.

Note:

### chunk_0b7ae8dd166147cc87a6fcf02f7929c1 (sequence 981)
- section_id: `sec_bbc175d476be436ba9bd1499565256cc`
- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.2 Running Gear > 8.2.2 Vibration damper on PTO, free end - Removal > Removing vibration damper`
- page range: `274`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Note: The hydraulic nut has the task of safely catching and cushioning the vibration damper when it slides off the taper seat.

Vent hand pump and pipework until bubblefree oil emerges.

Fill hand pumps with SAE 10W engine oil.

Tighten the HP line.

Read off maximum expansion pressure p max at vibration damper.

Actuate hand pump kit 700 bar (2) for hydraulic nut and, by applying minimum pressure p 2 (start of pressure increase), seat hydraulic nut against hub.

Actuate hand pump kit 3000 bar (1) for expanding vibration damper until half of the expansion pressure p 1 has been reached.

Increase expansion pressure in stages of 0.1 x p max , waiting approx. 2 minutes between increases, until the vibration damper is released from the crankshaft. Do not exceed maximum permissible expansion pressure p max .

Maintain pressure p 1 for approx. 5 minutes.

Continue to pump to keep the dropping expansion pressure constant.

Gradually drain oil in hydraulic nut, while continuing to pump expansion fluid at the same time.

Monitor pressure p 2 in hydraulic nut. The release of the vibration damper from the taper seat is indicated by an increase in pressure p 2 .

Relieve hand pumps.

Remove nut, hydraulic nut, thrust sleeve and mount.

Unscrew HP line.

Screw adapter (3) with the lifting bracket onto vibration damper (2).

If necessary remove vibration damper housing (1) as per overview drawing (→ Page 269).
```
