### chunk_cd8601a2c3294466a2069dcbe2190cf9 (sequence 993)
- section_id: `sec_062dafcb677e43b1841facb3d0d5573b`
- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.2 Running Gear > 8.2.3 Vibration damper on PTO free end - Installation > Press-fitting vibration damper`
- page range: `276 -> 277`
- chunk_type: `technical_specification`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: `picture_5a47a80984c743d4b6ee72e987c2f7be`
- content:
```text
Measure distance from inner vibration damper end face to spacer sleeve.
If measured value is less than push-on dimension 'a' (→ Page 269), check taper for dimensional accuracy.
TIM-ID: 0000011820 - 003
Screw reducer into the vibration damper and connect to HP line (2).
Set hydraulic nut (5) to initial position (zero stroke).
Push thrust sleeve (6) onto puller spindle.
Screw on nut (4) and tighten.
Connect HP line (3).
Fill hand pumps with SAE 10 engine oil.
Tighten the HP line.
Vent hand pump and pipework until bubblefree oil emerges.
Note: Prior to press-fitting, moisten tapers with expansion fluid.
Actuate 3000 bar hand pump kit (2) for the hydraulic nut to move the hydraulic nut up to the vibration damper using minimal pressure.
To do this, actuate 700 bar hand pump kit (1) until expansion fluid escapes at end of vibration damper.
Pump in expansion fluid until expansion pressure p 1 no longer rises. Then increase push-on force by raising force-on pressure p 2 .
Select a push-on force so that the end position is reached in approx. 5 steps.
```

```text
Repeat this procedure until the vibration damper reaches its final position.

Read off expansion pressure p max at vibration damper. Ensure that, during installation, the required expansion pressure is less than the maximum expansion pressure p max . A sudden rise in push-on pressure indicates that end position has been reached.

Reduce expansion pressure by loosening the valve screw of the hand pumps.

Result: Hydraulic installation is completed when thrust sleeve is seated against crankshaft.

Maintain maximum push-on pressure for 60 minutes, to ensure that the expansion fluid is expelled from the joint and static friction can build up between the fixed components.

Unscrew high-pressure line.
```

- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Place piston and conrod on workbench.

Using snap ring pliers (2), remove snap ring (1).

Check markings of conrod, piston and piston pin. If necessary, re-mark the components.

Use a piece of round wood to press out piston pin (2), holding conrod (1) firmly in position.

Remove conrod (1) from piston.
```

### chunk_5d11f048b47b4e65a4d3db8114c9a5ae (sequence 1032)
- section_id: `sec_28fe45c6afb642ed8ee9d170ca25c6d1`
- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.2 Running Gear > 8.2.8 Piston - Cleaning > Cleaning piston`
- page range: `289 -> 290`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Important

Observe the valid version of the Fluids and Lubricants Specifications. Further approved cleaning agents may be used.

|

|

Note: The graphite layer on the piston skirt must not come into contact with strong cleaning agents or be damaged/ removed mechanically.

Clean the piston ring groove area with a plastic brush.

Remove all deposits from functional and sealing surfaces.

Clean all functional and sealing surfaces with cleaner.

Remove corrosion inhibitor from new component using cleaner.

Wipe all functional and sealing surfaces dry with a clean, lint-free cloth.

After cleaning, blow off oil chamber and oil bores with compressed air.
```

```text
| Measure piston pin outside diame- ter with micrometer. Values (→ Page 293) | Values exceeded. | Replace piston pin. |
| Check piston rings. | • Piston rings burred, chipped or sharp-edged • If chrome layer shows scores, cracks or burn marks. | Replace |
```

```text
Measuring conrod basic bore with bearing shells

Assemble conrod (→ Page 300).

Coat sliding surfaces of bearing shells with engine oil.

Remove conrod screws, conrod cap and bearing shells.

Protect bearing shells from damage.

Measuring conrod bushing of conrod small end

Adjust bore gauge (1) to zero dimension of conrod bushing bore and measure conrod bushing bore (2). Values (→ Page 298).

If values are exceeded: Replace conrod.
```

### chunk_d2d27584a0534b689b5d1b1a271b7fa4 (sequence 1100)
- section_id: `sec_9600e0e79f3d487f80ceaad38decb028`
- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.2 Running Gear > 8.2.15 Piston and conrod - Installation`
- page range: `306 -> 307`
- chunk_type: `installation_instruction`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Install barring tool (→ Page 136).

Wipe crankpin and running surface of cylinder liner with chamois leather and spray with engine oil.

Move crankpin of respective cylinder on right side to 40° before TDC and on left side to 40° after TDC.

Preparing piston for installation

Spray piston and piston rings with engine oil.

Center piston rings and beveled oil-control ring in grooves.

Ensure that piston ring joints (arrowed) are evenly distributed at 120° around piston circumference.

Preparing conrod bearing for installation

Blow parting surfaces (arrows) on conrod bearing cap and conrod with compressed air and check for cleanness.

If necessary, wipe bearing shell mating faces on conrod and conrod cap with chamois leather.

Correctly assign conrod, conrod bearing cap (1) and conrod bearing shells (2) in accordance with the marking made during removal (→ Page 284).

Insert lower conrod bearing shell (2) with securing lug (arrowed) in groove of conrod bearing cap (1).
```

### chunk_71a70d3013f0451491cb9a8eebf76138 (sequence 1102)
- section_id: `sec_9600e0e79f3d487f80ceaad38decb028`
- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.2 Running Gear > 8.2.15 Piston and conrod - Installation`
- page range: `307 -> 308`
- chunk_type: `installation_instruction`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
|

Aligning conrod bearing shell

Align bearing shell (2) flush with joint faces.

Coat running surface of conrod bearing shell (2) with engine oil.

Press in conrod bearing shell (2) with alignment jig (1).

Installing piston and conrod in cylinder liner

Before installing piston and conrod (1) in cylinder liner (3), fit sliding block (2) on conrod (1) to be installed.

Note: In order to guide the conrod and avoid damage to the oil spray nozzle, installation of piston must be carried out by two persons. Install piston (1) without carbon scraper ring inserted.

Place mounting sleeve for piston (1) with chamfered side facing up on cylinder liner.

Install lifting rig (2) on piston (1).

Coat crankpin of crankshaft, mounting sleeve and cylinder liner with engine oil.

Mount conrod foot on crankpin of crankshaft and remove sliding block.

Insert piston (1) in cylinder liner such that the short arm of the conrod faces outward toward the air intake side. Twist piston (1) a little to avoid damaging oil spray nozzle.

Note: Note installation position in accordance with marking.

Carefully press conrod bearing cap onto conrod by hand.
```

### chunk_dcfec99ec6194c0798d65fb983fac70b (sequence 1105)
- section_id: `sec_d04394d8f56042fa93e66da83ab1ee18`
- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.2 Running Gear > 8.2.15 Piston and conrod - Installation > Installing conrod bearing cap`
- page range: `309`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Coat threads and screw head mating face of conrod bearing screws with engine oil.

Screw in conrod bearing screws up to screw head mating face and tighten firmly by hand using socket wrench, ensuring that conrod cap serrations are closed.

Insert conrod bearing screws into screw bore on conrod cap by hand and screw in by hand for the first three turns.

Note: Pay attention to axial movement of conrod when tightening.

Short arm

Use torque wrench to tighten conrod bearing screws to specified tightening torque. Tightening sequence:

Long arm

If one of the conrod bearing screws can be turned further before the checking torque is reached, loosen both conrod bearing screws and repeat the tightening procedure.

Detach lifting rig and mounting sleeve for piston and take off.

Check conrod for axial movement.

Crank crankshaft and ensure that there is ease of movement between oil spray nozzle, piston and conrod.
```

```text
Remove seal plug from oil supply bore and install lifting bracket (1).

Attach cylinder head (2) to crane with lifting bracket (1) and rope, ensuring that the rope is lightly tensioned.

Place cylinder head (2) via setting mandrels onto crankcase.

Coat threads, screw head mating faces and shanks of cylinder head screws (1) with engine oil.
```

### chunk_3383414cf874407ea1a81bf0ac1d7742 (sequence 1188)
- section_id: `sec_441cee6d5d2644fd8abbd9201d8325f9`
- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.4 Valve Gear > 8.4.6 Valve drive - Installation`

- chunk_type: `installation_instruction`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Coat ball seats and ball sockets of pushrods (1) with engine oil.

Mount valve bridges (2).

Insert pushrods (1) through cylinder head in ball seat of swing follower.

Installing rocker arm

Note: Take care not to damage fit of grooved pins.

Check position of ball joints in pushrods (1).

Place rocker shaft support at firing TDC onto cylinder head.

Install screw (4) with washer  (5).

After initial assembly or after long out-of-service period: Fill adjusting screws (3) with engine oil (arrowed) (→ Page 149).

Use a torque wrench to tighten screw (4) to specified tightening torque.

Turn adjusting screws (3) of rocker arms (6) in pushrod support until they just make contact.

Adjust valve clearance (→ Page 150).

Screw nuts (2) onto adjusting screws (3) and use a torque wrench to tighten to specified tightening torque.
```

- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.5 Fuel System (High Pressure) > 8.5.3 HP pump - Removal`

```text
Fuels are combustible and explosive.

Avoid open flames, electrical sparks and ignition sources.

Risk of fire and explosion!

Do not smoke.

Wear protective clothing, protective gloves, and safety glasses / facial protection.

Heavy part, risk of falling or overturning due to lack of stability.

Use appropriate lifting gear and appliances.

Risk of crushing body or limbs!

Wear safety shoes.

Hot components/surfaces.

Allow the system to cool down to below 50 °C before beginning work.

Risk of burns!

Wear suitable protective equipment/thermal gloves.

Avoid unprotected contact with hot surfaces.

Liquid or gaseous media, e.g. fuel, are poisonous.

Risk of fatal injury through swallowing; risk of poisoning through inhalation; irritation to eyes and skin!

Escaping vapors of highly volatile media, e.g. fuel or ether.

Seek medical attention immediately; do not induce vomiting.

Wear protective clothing, protective gloves, and safety glasses.

Do not inhale vapors or smoke.

If contact is made with skin, wash off with water and soap.

Keep the engine room well ventilated at all times.

Internal loads and residual pressures in the HP fuel system. Risk of flying parts when released. Risk of pressurized fuel spraying out.

Never work on the HP fuel system when the engine is running.

Risk of injury from flying parts and spraying fuel!
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_00ddc878cbcf4bd8839b83bcf85fb0ae (sequence 1202)
- section_id: `sec_0a54ca067ac54ee2a512ccd9d5fe7849`
- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.5 Fuel System (High Pressure) > 8.5.3 HP pump - Removal`
- page range: `341 -> 342`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Wait at least 15 mins. to relieve pressure before opening the HP fuel system.

Always wear protective goggles / safety mask.

Only use specified tools and jigs.

Undo threaded connections slowly.

Contamination of components.

Seal off components with suitable covers.

Risk of damage to component!

Check components for special cleanliness prior to installation/assembly and clean if necessary.

|

|

HP pump - Removal

Note: Note the system pressure: The residual pressure in the HP fuel system after engine stop and a 10 minute waiting time is approx. 25 bar.

Remove oil line (1) to high-pressure pump (2).

Note: Hold adapter in place.

Remove retainer as shown in overview drawing (→ Page 339).

Loosen HP fuel line.

Unscrew securing screws except for topmost screw as shown in overview drawing (→ Page 339).

Screw adjusting mandrel (1) into bore of HP pump (2).

Mark bore with adjusting mandrel (1).

Install adapter (1) on HP pump (3).

Attach lifting bracket (2) to crane.

Install adapter (1) on lifting bracket (2) and lock with ball locking pin.

Unscrew topmost securing screw.

Remove HP pump (3) via adjusting mandrel.
```

```text
Install fuel distributor (2) on raw water cooler such that there is no movement in the direction of the crankshaft.

Coat O-ring for adapter (4) with assembly compound.

Seal off interfaces on fuel distributor with caps to prevent dirt ingress until the various components are going to be installed.

Install adapter (4) on HP pump with O-ring and use a torque wrench to tighten to specified tightening torque.

Coat HP lines (3), (5) and (6) on threads, sealing cones, thrust rings and jacket surface with engine oil ensuring that the O-ring inside is also wetted.

Coat O-rings with assembly compound.

Install caps for threading in, but disassemble once again prior to final assembly.

Note:

Assembly is a two-man job.

Slide the union nuts/screws as far back as possible when applying to the sealing cone.

Avoid damaging sealing surfaces when threading.

Remove sleeves from HP accumulator, coat O-rings with assembly compound and install with HP line on HP accumulator observing the direction of installation.

HP line to rail A-side (3)

Thread in HP lines (3), (5) and (6) in the following order:

HP line to HP pump (5)

Tighten union nuts evenly until the sealing faces make noticeable contact in the sealing cone at both ends of the line.

HP line to rail B-side (6)
```

```text
Place screws (3) and (4) for holder on raw water cooler evenly in position such that the contact surfaces are flat and align camlock grommets.

Coat sealing cone, thread and under screw head of pressure relief valve (4) with engine oil.

Coat O-ring with assembly compound.
```

```text
8.6.2 Fuel delivery pump - Preparatory steps

Preconditions

☑ Engine is stopped and starting disabled.

Preparatory steps

Remove air supply pipework to the cylinders on left side (→ Page 438).

Remove fuel lines of fuel delivery pump (→ Page 370).

8.6.3 Fuel delivery pump - Removal

Preconditions

☑ Preparatory steps have been completed.

Fuels are combustible and explosive.

Avoid open flames, electrical sparks and ignition sources.

Risk of fire and explosion!

Do not smoke.

Wear protective clothing, protective gloves, and safety glasses / facial protection.

Liquid or gaseous media, e.g. fuel, are poisonous. Escaping vapors of highly volatile media, e.g. fuel or ether.

Seek medical attention immediately; do not induce vomiting.

Risk of fatal injury through swallowing; risk of poisoning through inhalation; irritation to eyes and skin!

Do not inhale vapors or smoke.

If contact is made with skin, wash off with water and soap.

Wear protective clothing, protective gloves, and safety glasses.

Keep the engine room well ventilated at all times.

Fuel delivery pump - Removal

Remove screws (2) with washers (1).

Remove fuel delivery pump from equipment carrier.
```

```text
Suspended load.

Use suitable equipment and lifting devices. Lifting by crane must only be carried out by qualified personnel.

Danger to life!
```

```text
Remove the oil return lines before installing the exhaust turbochargers. The flexible part of the oil return lines must not be bent, stretched or otherwise damaged.

Exhaust turbocharger - Installation

Install carrier housing on exhaust turbocharger (→ Page 458).

Degrease and dry-clean bolt-on faces on carrier housing and exhaust housing.

Remove cover.

Note: Apply silicone rubber surface sealant directly before assembly. Surface sealant must not have started to dry.

Apply a bead of silicone rubber (arrow) approx. 5 mm wide and 3 mm thick to mating face of exhaust housing.
```

### chunk_4d23f547baee41e2a096d1a62de7babc (sequence 1528)
- section_id: `sec_0fbcda349589435c8757a16096b482da`
- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.11 Exhaust Pipework > 8.11.4 Exhaust pipework after cylinder head - Installation > Installing exhaust housing`
- page range: `452`
- chunk_type: `technical_specification`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
|
Coat O-rings of flanges on coolant distribution housing with assembly compound.
Coat O-rings (1) with assembly compound.
Clean bolt-on faces on cylinder heads to ensure they are free from grease and dry.
Insert O-rings (1) in recesses on cylinder heads.
The distance of the silicone rubber to the exhaust outlet opening at the cylinder head must be approx. 10 mm.
Apply silicone rubber directly before installation. The silicone rubber must not become touch dry.
Apply a bead of silicone rubber (arrowed) approx. 4 mm wide and 3 mm thick to mating face.
Coat screws for exhaust housing with engine oil.
Position exhaust housing and insert in flanges on coolant distribution housing.
Insert screws with washers and tighten crosswise.
Note: Only if the exhaust housing was disassembled beforehand:
Tighten screws of the exhaust pipework segments to specified tightening torque.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

### chunk_50720744380f426388326b0d730fbb6e (sequence 1530)
- section_id: `sec_c81e1b987767438aa6d6dcade4061ab6`
- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.11 Exhaust Pipework > 8.11.4 Exhaust pipework after cylinder head - Installation > Installing exhaust pipe bellows`
- page range: `453`
- chunk_type: `installation_instruction`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Place cover (4) onto opening in exhaust pipework (5).

Place insertion jig (6) onto blind flange (7). Make sure that the insertion jig (6) fully rests on blind flange (7).

Use centering pin (3) to place insertion jig (2) onto cover (4).

Apply assembly compound to insertion jigs (2, 6).

Note: Observe the flow direction, which is indicated as an arrow at the flange of the bellows (see figure).

Insert exhaust pipe bellows (1) between insertion jigs (2, 6) and align flanges.

Screw on exhaust pipe bellows (2) with two screws (4) and two washers (5) on A-side and B-side. Do not tighten screws (4) firmly.

Remove cover (3).

Pull out insertion jigs (1).

Screw in screws (2) with washers (1).

Tighten all screws to the specified tightening torque.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none

```text
Attach exhaust turbocharger (4) to crane with the rope slightly pretensioned.

Remove nuts (3) and take off washer (2).

Remove nuts (5) and take off dished washers (6).

Take care not to damage turbine blades and lift exhaust turbocharger (4) from carrier housing (8,10).

Remove O-ring.

Fit protective cap on turbocharger (4).

Remove screws (7).

Remove screws (1).

Set assembled carrier housing (8, 10) aside on a suitable base. Take care not to damage studs.

Lift off carrier housing (10).

Fit spacer sleeves for transportation onto studs of turbine housing (9).

Lift off turbine housing (9).

Lift off carrier housing (8).

Seal all openings with suitable covers.

Fit spacer sleeves for transportation onto studs of turbine housing (9).
```

### chunk_e86fe24de07a453ba2b9f140342e365f (sequence 1548)
- section_id: `sec_4c34efadefff4e7fa4ae3bbcda8a323f`
- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.11 Exhaust Pipework > 8.11.9 Carrier housing - Installation > Installing carrier housing on exhaust turbocharger`
- page range: `458 -> 459`
- chunk_type: `general`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
|

Insert turbine housing (2) in inner half (3) of carrier housing.

Coat O-ring (1) with assembly compound and fit on turbine housing (2).

Degrease and dry-clean flange faces on both parts of the carrier housing.

Insert restrictors (3) as shown in overview drawing or according to markings in carrier housing (→ Page 455).

Insert suitable guide pins into carrier housing.

Note: Apply silicone rubber directly before installation. The silicone rubber must not become touch dry.

Position outer half (1) of carrier housing over guide pins.

Coat flange faces on both parts of the carrier housing with silicone rubber.

Coat threads of screws (2) with engine oil.

Insert screws (2) and tighten.

Coat studs on turbine housing and on carrier housing (1) with engine oil.

Coat O-ring (7) with assembly compound and insert in groove on bearing housing.

Coat O-ring (8) with assembly compound and fit on bearing housing of the exhaust turbocharger (4).

Assemble carrier housing (1) and exhaust turbocharger (4).

Screw nuts (5) with washers (6) on studs of carrier housing (1).
```

- content:
```text
Suspended load.

Use suitable equipment and lifting devices. Lifting by crane must only be carried out by qualified personnel.

Danger to life!

Never stand beneath a suspended load and keep a safe distance.

Wear personal protective equipment (e.g. protective helmet, safety shoes).

Compressed-air pipes may still be under pressure, although the shut-off valve is closed.

Before starting work, release pressure from pipework.

Risk of injury!

Hot components/surfaces.

Allow the system to cool down to below 50 °C before beginning work.

Risk of burns!

Wear suitable protective equipment/thermal gloves.

Avoid unprotected contact with hot surfaces.

Heavy part, risk of falling or overturning due to lack of stability.

Use appropriate lifting gear and appliances.

Risk of crushing body or limbs!

Wear safety shoes.

Starter - Removal

Remove pressure hose.

Remove starter as per overview drawing (→ Page 465).

Attach starter (3) to crane with the ropes slightly tensioned.

Lift starter off the flange.

Set down starter and protect it from damage and ingress of foreign bodies.
```

- section_id: `sec_9c698ac97d66478cbfc9a16f24bf925b`
- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.12 Starting Equipment > 8.12.6 Starter - Installation > Installing starter`
- page range: `470`
- chunk_type: `installation_instruction`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Coat starter pinion with lubricating grease and turn pinion back into initial position if necessary.

Insert starter in opening on flywheel housing.

Attach starter to crane.

Align location bores on starter with mounting bores.

Detach starter from crane.

Install starter as per overview drawing (→ Page 465).

Wrap two layers of Teflon sealing tape around thread surface of adapter unions (1) for starter connection.

Screw in adapter union (1) of starter connection and tighten to specified tightening torque.

Connect pressure hose to starter.

Check operation of starter.
```

- content:

```text
Wear safety shoes.
Coolant contains antifreeze and is toxic.
Avoid contact with eyes and skin.
Do not inhale vapors or mist, wear breathing protection.
Wear protective clothing, protective gloves and goggles/safety mask.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when working with antifreeze.
Wipe up escaped/spilled coolant immediately.
Components have sharp edges.
Wear protective gloves.
A
|
Remove all covers.
Insert O-ring (1) in groove on bearing housing of engine coolant pump.
Coat O-ring (1) with assembly compound.
Install adapter (2) with lifting bracket (1) on engine coolant pump and attach to crane using a round sling, ensuring that the sling is lightly tensioned.
Note: Position engine coolant pump such that backlash is provided.
Insert screws (3) with washers and tighten evenly.
Insert engine coolant pump in correct position in mount on equipment carrier while observing gear engagement.
Remove adapter (2) with lifting bracket (1).
|
```

```text
Tighten drain valve with 2 rotations.

Tighten shut-off cock (2) with torque wrench to specified tightening torque.
```

```text
Coolant cooler and fuel cooler - Removal

Mark cooler plates with numbers or identify accordingly to ensure correct installation sequence for subsequent assembly.

Insert guide pieces.

Remove cover plate and cooler plate individually via guide pieces as shown in overview drawing (→ Page 506).

Remove remaining screws alternately two turns each until the plate stack is released.

Place cooler plates to the side and protect from damage.

Seal openings with suitable covers.

Note:

Sequence is arbitrary

Note:

Undo all screws by 90°.

Sequence is arbitrary

Note:

Remove screws (1), (3), (5), (7), (9), (10), (12), (14), (16), (18), (20), (21).

Removal sequence: (22), (11), (19), (8), (2), (13), (17), (6), (15), (4)
```

```text
Insert screw (8) on all engine supports (1) until they make full contact on foundation. Place an adequately strong spacer underneath if necessary.

Loosen nut (7) on all engine supports (1).

Result: Engine is blocked against compression of the resilient mounts.

Unscrew nuts (3) with washers (4) from threaded pin (2).

Lock screw (8) with nut (7) on all engine supports (1).

Remove screws (5) with washers (6).
```

### chunk_65692fdced61463e93925fc852f5ecb1 (sequence 1825)
- section_id: `sec_0374f5101b244fffbc6993874f50ae74`
- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.15 Mounting / Support > 8.15.3 Engine mounting - Removal`
- page range: `547 -> 548`
- chunk_type: `installation_instruction`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
|

|

Screw studs (8) into base plate of resilient mount.

Screw on nuts (7) and fit washers (9).

Screw on nuts (5) together with washers (6) and fix studs (8) with locknut.

Mount locking parts (10) and (2) screw on nuts (3) with washers (4) until they make contact with the locking part (2).

Result: Resilient mount is secured against compression and the height dimension is retained.

Screw nuts (7) from below against blocking parts (10) and (2) and tighten them.

Loosen adjusting screw (1) a few rotations to guarantee ease of movement between resilient mount and adjusting screw (1).

Remove locked resilient mount with suitable lifting gear between base frame and engine mounting bracket.

Removing engine mounting bracket

Attach engine mounting bracket (1) to crane with a lightly tensioned rope.

Remove engine mounting bracket (1) from crankcase.

Remove screws (3) and thrust washer (2).

Remove profile gasket from rear side of engine mounting bracket (1).

Seal inspection port with a suitable cover.

Removing engine support

Note: Remove engine support only if necessary. Ensure that supports are not stressed by engine.

Remove engine support from crankcase.

Remove screws and washers on engine support.
```

### chunk_9552c5e24d514ffb98efeb0c235c6838 (sequence 1838)
- section_id: `sec_3295ebf50de64459837d15655a3ce22f`
- section_path: `8 Instructions for Exchange of Sub-assemblies > 8.15 Mounting / Support > 8.15.4 Engine mounting - Installation > Installing resilient mounts`
- page range: `551`
- chunk_type: `installation_instruction`
- table_ids: ``
- picture_ids: ``
- content:
```text
Clean and degrease flange-mounting surfaces of resilient mount, foundation, and adjusting screw.

Coat screws (2) with engine oil.

Use suitable lifting equipment to insert locked resilient mount (4) between foundation and engine mounting bracket and align it to the bores in the foundation.

Manually insert screws (2) with washers (3).

Coat threaded pins (1) with engine oil.

Insert threaded pin (1) into resilient mount and use torque wrench to tighten to specified tightening torque.

Screw in adjusting screw (1) as far as the stop on resilient mount.

Screw on nuts (2) with washers (3) and tighten to specified torque using a torque wrench.

Release upper nuts on locking device (6) alternately and evenly.

Remove locking device (6) with studs, nuts and washers from resilient mount.

Install screws (4) with washers (5) and use a torque wrench to tighten to specified tightening torque.

Release nut (7) and back off screw (8) on all engine supports (9) until there is sufficient clearance to the foundation.
```
- outgoing cross-references: none
